A hook is required because the permission rule engine cannot carve an allow exception out of a broader deny.
sheets.rejected_alternative: settings.json permissions with deny Bash(aws:*) plus allow Bash(aws s3 ls:*): deny rules take precedence over allow rules, so the broad deny swallows the exception and aws s3 ls gets refused too.
sheets.enforcement_owner: Harness: the hook decision is applied before execution and the model cannot negotiate around it.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook process inspects the command string from stdin outside the context window; only the allow or deny outcome and any denial reason surface to the model.
sheets.lifecycle: Runs on every Bash tool call for the session while configured; distribute via project or managed settings so it applies to every teammate.
sheets.failure_mode: Command parsing is the risk: compound commands like aws s3 ls && aws s3 rb, full binary paths, shell variables, or aws called inside a script must all be handled or the control fails open; a strict parser that denies anything ambiguous fails closed, which is the safer default here.
sheets.version_caveat: PreToolUse permissionDecision allow/deny/ask is the current 2025 hook output contract; older builds used the approve/block spelling, and I cannot pin the exact version boundary unaided.

sheets.primary: A PreToolUse hook on matcher Bash whose script denies (permissionDecision "deny") any subcommand starting with aws unless it is exactly aws s3 ls, paired with an allow rule Bash(aws s3 ls) so the approved invocation runs without prompting. The hook is required because permission rules alone cannot express a carve-out from a deny.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Pure permission rules, deny Bash(aws *) plus allow Bash(aws s3 ls): the docs use this exact aws example to show it cannot work, because deny is evaluated first and a deny rule cannot carry allowlist exceptions, so the approved command would be blocked too.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness: it runs the PreToolUse hook before every Bash call and a blocking hook takes precedence over allow rules, so refusal does not depend on the model.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook runs outside the context window; on a deny, the permissionDecisionReason is shown to Claude inside its context so it stops retrying, while the approved aws s3 ls result returns as a normal tool result.
sheets.lifecycle: The hook fires before every Bash tool call and the allow rule is evaluated in the same permission pass on each call; both apply for as long as they exist in loaded settings.
sheets.failure_mode: If implemented as rules only, it fails closed the wrong way (the approved command is blocked); with the hook, the script must handle compound commands and substitutions itself, and a parsing miss lets an aws call fall through to the normal permission flow, a prompt rather than an outright refusal, so the refusal guarantee fails open on unparsed shapes.
sheets.version_caveat: A hook deny has always been honored across documented versions; before v2.1.211 the auto-mode classifier could approve a command without showing a prompt a hook requested via ask, which is why the enforcement here uses deny, not ask.

sheets.primary: A PreToolUse command hook on Bash (if: "Bash(aws *)") that returns permissionDecision "deny" for any aws invocation, including each subcommand of compound commands, unless the command is exactly "aws s3 ls"; pair it with an allow rule "Bash(aws s3 ls)" so the approved call runs without prompting.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Pure permission rules, deny "Bash(aws *)" plus allow "Bash(aws s3 ls)": deny is evaluated before allow, so the broad deny blocks the narrower allowed call too; a deny rule cannot carry an allowlist exception.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness: the hook's deny decision blocks the call before the permission prompt, and hook blocks take precedence over allow rules.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook inspects the full command JSON outside the model context; only the deny reason crosses back so Claude can adjust course.
sheets.lifecycle: Runs on every Bash tool call matching the aws pattern for the life of the settings entry; the if filter deliberately fails open on unparseable commands so the script still gets to inspect them.
sheets.failure_mode: Degrades rather than breaks: if the hook script itself crashes, that is a non-blocking error and the call falls through to the normal permission flow, where non-allowlisted aws commands prompt instead of being refused outright; the script must itself check compound commands and $() substitutions rather than trusting the best-effort if filter.
sheets.version_caveat: No significant version gate; the documented Bash if-matching table governs when the handler spawns, and the sample stdin-parsing pattern needs jq (or a PowerShell equivalent) on PATH.

sheets.primary: A PreToolUse hook (matcher Bash, if: "Bash(aws *)") that parses tool_input.command and returns hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision "allow" for exactly aws s3 ls and "deny" for every other aws invocation. A hook is required because permission rules alone cannot express deny-all-with-one-exception: deny is evaluated first, so a broad deny rule cannot carry an allowlist carve-out, and an ask rule would violate the no-prompt requirement.
sheets.rejected_alternative: Permission rules deny Bash(aws *) plus allow Bash(aws s3 ls): the deny wins on every aws call including s3 ls, so the exception is inexpressible in rules alone.
sheets.enforcement_owner: The harness: the hook's allow/deny decision is enforced by the permission flow before the tool runs, and a matching managed deny rule would still take precedence over a hook allow.
sheets.context_boundary: The hook runs as a separate process before the tool executes; the command JSON crosses in on stdin, the permissionDecision JSON crosses out, and the deny reason is shown to Claude in context so it stops retrying blocked variants.
sheets.lifecycle: Runs before every matching Bash tool call for the life of the configuration; it stops when the hook is removed or hooks are disabled, so ship it in managed settings (with allowManagedHooksOnly) if it must survive developer tampering.
sheets.failure_mode: Deny decisions fail closed, but command matching is best-effort string analysis: the if filter deliberately fails open (runs the hook) on unparseable commands, so the script must itself default to deny for any aws invocation it cannot classify; evasions such as running aws from inside a generated shell script bypass inspection of the literal command. A hook that crashes exits non-2 and is non-blocking, so always emit explicit decision JSON.
sheets.version_caveat: Use hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision with allow/deny/ask; the old top-level approve/block values are deprecated for PreToolUse and map to allow/deny.
